question.problem:
$$ \{\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}^{′}(t)=2{x}_{1}(t) \\ {x}_{2}^{′}(t)=3{x}_{1}(t)-{x}_{2}(t),\end{aligned}\,x(0)=[\begin{aligned}5 \\ 7\end{aligned}] $$ Consider the initial value problem above. By applying the Laplace transform to both sides of each equation in our system, we get a transformed system with the solution $$ {X}_{1}(s)=L\{{x}_{1}(t)\}=\frac{5}{s-2},\,{X}_{2}(s)=L\{{x}_{2}(t)\}=\frac{5}{s-2}+\frac{2}{s+1}. $$ Find the solution to the original initial value problem.
$x(t)=\,\,$ {{field-1}} $\,\,{e}^{2t}+\,\,$ {{field-2}} $\,\,{e}^{-t}$
{{field-3}} {{field-4}}
question.worked_solution:
To find ${x}_{1}(t)$ and ${x}_{2}(t)$ satisfying the original initial value problem, we apply the inverse Laplace transform to ${X}_{1}(s)$ and ${X}_{2}(s):$

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}(t) & ={L}^{-1}\{{X}_{1}(s)\} \\  & ={L}^{-1}\{\frac{5}{s-2}\} \\  & =5\,{L}^{-1}\{\frac{1}{s-2}\} \\  & =5{e}^{2\cdot t} \\  & =5{e}^{2t} \\ {x}_{2}(t) & ={L}^{-1}\{{X}_{2}(s)\} \\  & ={L}^{-1}\{\frac{5}{s-2}+\frac{2}{s+1}\} \\  & =5\,{L}^{-1}\{\frac{1}{s-2}\}+2\,{L}^{-1}\{\frac{1}{s+1}\} \\  & =5{e}^{2\cdot t}+2{e}^{-1\cdot t} \\  & =5{e}^{2t}+2{e}^{-t}\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we write down the solution to the initial value problem:

$$
\begin{aligned}x(t) & =[\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}(t) \\ {x}_{2}(t)\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}5{e}^{2t} \\ 5{e}^{2t}+2{e}^{-t}\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}5 \\ 5\end{aligned}]{e}^{2t}+[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 2\end{aligned}]{e}^{-t}\end{aligned}
$$
